CAP. XVI.
Q[?]VONIAM de Argumētatione Dia-
lectica satis dictum est, superest vt de
sophistica differamus. Ac primum
omnium quid est Sophistice? Falsa
doctrinæ simulatio. nam Sophistæ dicebātur
(inquit Aristoteles) qui ex ea quam præ se fe-
rebant fucata & adulterina sapientia quæstū
faciebant. quales nostris temporibus Rabu-
las forenses numerare possumus. Cicero au-
tè lib.de Finib.2. ita definit: Sophistæ (inquit)
dicebantur, qui ostentationis & quæstus caus-
a philosophabantur. Itaque Sophistice defi-
niri fic poteft, Captario[?] verborum quę dispu-
tandi prudentiam fallaciter imitando adul-
terat. Nam eodem modo Sophisticæ argumē-
tationes à Dialecticis differunt, quo adulte-
rini numi à probis. Sophismata autem Sene-
ca in Epistolis scribit, Cauillationes à Cicero-
ne Latinè appellari.
Quisnam huius doctrinæ est vsus? Idé pla-
nè, qui in mercatorum & argentariorum vi-
ta percipitur ex facultate probos numos ab
adulterinis internoscendi: aut aurum abori-
chalco: vel argentum à Lytargyrina. Cauen-

page.notes: Running head and signature read as printed. The word "nā-" at the line end is followed by "vt", so the joined word is doubtful. The woodcut initial is worn: the first letter is probably Q. "Captario" and "autè" are doubtful. The right-hand page is not on this scan.
